fields.sections.4.exchanges.1.pro.words: Cliffe Knechtle argues that Numbers 25 explains why Numbers 31 spared young girls for communal protection, not rape, because they lacked the adult women’s culpability.
fields.sections.4.exchanges.1.pro.critique: Strongest feature: Knechtle directly answers the rape allegation by linking Numbers 31 to Numbers 25, distinguishing culpable adult women from spared younger girls whom he says entered protective communal care. Principal limitation: neither that context nor any quoted language establishes his age generalization, collective culpability, protective purpose, noncoercive reception, or release from the passage’s classification of captives as plunder. Live burden: Knechtle must show that sparing these girls legally and practically entailed provision within the community rather than ownership, forced dependency, or another coercive status fully compatible with survival. Locked score: 60 recognizes a clear, relevant alternative to the rape interpretation and direct engagement with this central case, while withholding stronger credit because the decisive transition from being spared to being protected remains textually unsupported and rhetorically overstated.
